title: St. Peter's lands $49K grant for a bird-watching nature program
summary: St. Peter's Episcopal Church won a $49,000 United Thank Offering grant to expand its Sprout Reach conservation ministry with a nature-journaling curriculum built around birding. The church is developing it with the Green Valleys Watershed Association and plans to bring it to youth camps and to Floctoberfest in October.

title: Amtrak deal moves a Phoenixville train stop closer to reality
summary: Amtrak and the Schuylkill River Passenger Rail Authority signed an agreement to plan and develop passenger service linking Reading, Pottstown, Phoenixville and Philadelphia, a corridor with no trains since 1981. Officials put the rail portion near $100 million and say service could start around 2030.

title: Broadway veterans bring an Alzheimer's benefit play to the Colonial
summary: Dan Lauria and Patty McCormack will stage their play about memory and aging, Just Another Day, at the Colonial Theatre Sept. 25 through 27. Both actors are donating their performances, with proceeds going to the Alzheimer's Association and the theater.

title: Cat adoption room coming to a Bridge Street pet boutique
summary: Calla's Kitty Kingdom, a permanent adoption space for rescue cats, was slated to open in late August inside Maddie's Castle at 178 Bridge Street. Calla's Critter Rescue supplies the cats, Maddie's Castle the storefront, and BarkHop Studio photographs the animals for adoption listings.

title: Valley Forge Self Storage changes hands
summary: Marcus & Millichap brokered the sale of the 415-unit Valley Forge Self Storage on S. 2nd Avenue to Manas Equities. The 2005-built facility covers 7.8 acres near Route 23 and the Schuylkill River, with climate-controlled and drive-up units plus covered parking.

title: Ocean State Job Lot nears opening at Shoppes at Valley Forge
summary: The discount chain is filling a 29,525-square-foot former Big Lots at the Shoppes at Valley Forge, its first store in Chester County. Walk-in hiring ran through mid-August and the opening is targeted for after Labor Day.

title: University of Valley Forge closing after 87 years
summary: The private Christian university in Phoenixville will suspend academic operations at the end of its Summer 2026 semester, ending an 87-year run. Trustees cited years of financial strain and an accreditation warning, and the school is helping students transfer.
